items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: As a matter of fact I did play a lot at the end of his career with him.

ctx.x: Did that translate into the number of dates you would accept in one day? I remember, I was lucky enough to have a conversation with Joe Wilder, who did a lot in New York. And he would comment, he didn’t name names, but that people would accept multiple dates in a day knowing they weren’t going to be able to get to the third one on time.

You used to be able to get away with that at one point in this town. I mean there was a time when there was a lot of work and there was a lot of very high demand players, players that were doing everything, doing all the pop recording and just doing several sessions a day. And they’d take a 10:00 that’s supposed to go to 1:00 and then there’d be a 1:30 date across town and they would take it in hopes that they were going to get out early. And sometimes they were. And many times they’d go, “Oh we’re always done…

started late on. So a lot of these players, like people just expected them to be late. That does not exist anymore. And it’s a little bit greedy you know. I won’t say I’ve never been guilty of like threading the needle. Because when they call you for a recording session, a three hour session is standard. Like 10:00 to 1:00 is standard, right? So if you’re going to do a double session it would be 10:00 to 1:00 with an hour lunch break, and then 2:00 to 5:00. So let’s say you were doing just the 10:00 to 1:00 that…
